---
title: "Wavesurfer HDF5"
---

[Wavesurfer](https://wavesurfer.janelia.org/) saves continuous acquisition data in HDF5 `.h5` files. Neuralyzer can load **bit-packed digital TTL scans** from datasets such as `sweep_0001/digitalScans`, plus an **identity master clock** derived from the dataset shape.

## File layout

Typical structure:

| Path | Description |
|---|---|
| `header/AcquisitionSampleRate` | DAQ rate in Hz (e.g. 250000) |
| `header/DIChannelNames` | Digital input names (e.g. `cam`, `pulse_pal`) |
| `sweep_XXXX/digitalScans` | Packed TTL samples (`uint8` on disk) |
| `sweep_XXXX/timestamp` | Sweep timestamp metadata |

### uint8 storage vs uint16 semantics

Wavesurfer stores `digitalScans` as **`uint8`**, but each sample is a **uint16 TTL word** via zero-extension (the same as `astype(np.uint16)` in NumPy). Values 0–3 use bits 0 and 1 for the two digital inputs:

| Bit | Typical channel |
|---|---|
| 0 | Camera TTL (`cam`, DI0) |
| 1 | PulsePal TTL (`pulse_pal`, DI1) |

This is **not** byte-pair reinterpretation — two `uint8` bytes are not combined into one sample.

## Loading digital events and intervals

Bit-packed loading requires `data_key`, `channel` (bit index), and `transition` (`rising` or `falling`). Event and interval times are **DAQ sample indices**.

```json
{
  "name": "cam_ttl",
  "format": "hdf5",
  "data_type": "digital_event",
  "filepath": "/path/to/recording.h5",
  "data_key": "sweep_0001/digitalScans",
  "channel": 0,
  "transition": "rising",
  "clock": "master"
}
```

```json
{
  "name": "pulse_pal_intervals",
  "format": "hdf5",
  "data_type": "digital_interval",
  "filepath": "/path/to/recording.h5",
  "data_key": "sweep_0001/digitalScans",
  "channel": 1,
  "transition": "rising",
  "clock": "master"
}
```

For 2D datasets shaped `(rows, samples)`, optional `sweep_row` (default `0`) selects which row to read.

## Clock assignment

Declare clocks and build a master + camera-frame timebase:

```json
{
  "clocks": ["master", "time"],
  "data": [
    {
      "name": "master",
      "format": "hdf5",
      "data_type": "time",
      "filepath": "/path/to/recording.h5",
      "data_key": "sweep_0001/digitalScans",
      "time_layout": "identity"
    },
    {
      "name": "cam_ttl",
      "format": "hdf5",
      "data_type": "digital_event",
      "filepath": "/path/to/recording.h5",
      "data_key": "sweep_0001/digitalScans",
      "channel": 0,
      "transition": "rising",
      "clock": "master"
    },
    {
      "format": "derived",
      "data_type": "time",
      "name": "time",
      "source_timeframe": "master",
      "source_series": "cam_ttl",
      "source_type": "event"
    }
  ]
}
```

- **`master`**: identity ticks `[0, 1, …, N-1]` at the DAQ sample rate (shape-only read; fast).
- **`time`**: camera frame times derived from `cam_ttl` rising edges sampling `master`.

Bind video to `"clock": "time"`. PulsePal intervals remain on `master` (sample indices).

::: {.callout-note}
Converting sample indices to camera frame indices (as in a Jupyter workflow that estimates FPS from the camera TTL) is a downstream transform, not part of the loader.
:::
